results.title: America's Hidden Epidemic: The Deadliest Misdiagnoses ...
results.content: 2026 Forecast: 7.4 Million Diagnostic Errors, 795,000 Serious HarmsBased on current trends and 130 million annual emergency department visits, we project approximately 7.4 million diagnostic errors in 2026, resulting in 2.6 million cases of preventable harm and 795,000 Americans suffering death or permanent disability. **Who’s Most at Risk:** Young adults (doctors don’t suspect stroke), women (symptoms dismissed as anxiety), people presenting with “atypical” symptoms (dizziness, nausea, vertigo instead of paralysis), and patients at hospitals with low stroke volume where staff lack pattern recognition. 100-Fold Variation in Error Rates Across HospitalsThe same patient with the same symptoms presenting at different hospitals can face wildly different diagnostic accuracy. **Most Likely 2026 Outcome:** Incremental improvement in some areas (heart attack diagnosis, stroke recognition in high-volume centers), persistent or worsening errors in others (rare conditions, low-resource hospitals, complex multi-system diseases). **Is this acceptable?** No. Research shows that reducing diagnostic errors by 50% for just five conditions (stroke, sepsis, pneumonia, blood clots, lung cancer) would prevent 150,000 deaths and disabilities per year.
